equation_request.abstract: The effects of imperfect gate operations in implementation of Shor's prime factorization algorithm are investigated. The gate imperfections may be classified into three categories: the systematic error, the random error, and the one with combined errors. It is found that Shor's algorithm is robust against the systematic errors but is vulnerable to the random errors. Error threshold is given to the algorithm for a given number N to be factorized.

specification.problem: Simulate Shor order finding for a small N (N=15, a=7, order r=4) with gate-angle imperfections (systematic, random, combined), and measure the success probability versus epsilon or sigma. Then estimate an error threshold. The abstract states only the qualitative findings: robust to systematic errors, vulnerable to random errors, and an N-dependent threshold.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One instance: N=15, a=7, n=4 work qubits, t=8 counting qubits (12 qubits total; t could be reduced to fit a smaller cap). Ideal circuit plus an angle-perturbation noise model on QFT controlled-phase and Rz gates. Out of scope: the paper's actual error model, analytic threshold formula, and any numerical values. The abstract does not give them.

symbols.meaning: number of work qubits, ceil(log2 N)
multiplicative order of a mod N
integer read from counting register, with qubit 0 as the least significant bit
standard deviation of random angle error
relative angle shift on gate g
symbols.domain: real; equals epsilon, a Gaussian draw with std sigma, or the sum of both

equations.label: Order-finding state
equations.description: Modular multiplication unitary, and the state after H on the counting register and the controlled U_a^(2^k) gates, with the work register starting in |1>.
equations.justification: Textbook Shor construction; the abstract only names Shor's algorithm.
assumptions: U_a is defined as a permutation on y<N and identity on y>=N

equations.label: Ideal peak distribution
equations.description: After the inverse QFT, the counting register is concentrated near multiples of 2^t/r. For r=4 and t=8 the ideal peaks are exactly m=0,64,128,192.
equations.justification: Standard result, applicable when r divides 2^t.

equations.label: Noisy gate model
equations.description: Angle perturbations applied to the QFT controlled-phase gates. Optionally an extra Rz(delta) is applied after each gate.
equations.justification: The sketch proposes this model. The abstract gives only the three categories, not the form of the error.
assumptions: Errors act on the QFT gates and Hadamards only, while modular multiplication is kept ideal
Random errors are i.i.d. per gate

equations.label: Success probability
equations.latex: P_s=\mathbb E_{\delta}\sum_{m}P_\delta(m)\,\mathbf 1[\text{postprocessing}(m)\text{ yields a nontrivial factor}]
equations.description: Average over sampled noisy circuits, with the exact statevector distribution for each. For systematic error a single circuit suffices.
equations.justification: Defines the metric. The abstract implies the algorithm's success is compared across error types.
assumptions: Exact statevector probabilities are used, with no sampling shot noise

equations.label: Threshold scaling heuristic
equations.description: Heuristic: random errors add incoherently, so fidelity loss scales as G sigma^2. The threshold is the sigma at which P_s falls to a chosen fraction of its ideal value.
equations.abstract_quote: Error threshold is given to the algorithm for a given number N to be factorized.
equations.justification: The abstract implies an N-dependent threshold. The 1/sqrt(G) form is a heuristic from the sketch, not stated in the abstract.
assumptions: The drop criterion (e.g. 50% of ideal) is a free choice

registers.name: count
registers.role: phase-estimation counting register, measured; qubit i has weight 2^i

registers.name: work
registers.role: holds a^x mod N, starting in |1>=|0001>; not measured

steps.description: Apply H to all counting qubits.
For k=0..t-1, apply U_7^(2^k) controlled on counting qubit k. For a=7 mod 15, powers are 7, 4, 1, 1... so only k=0 and k=1 are nontrivial and the rest are identities. Build from CSWAP/CX and X gates.
Apply the inverse QFT to the counting register using H, CP and SWAP gates. In the noisy runs, perturb each CP angle per the noise model.
Compute P_s versus epsilon, sigma and combined settings by averaging over sampled noisy circuits. Find sigma where P_s falls to the chosen fraction of the ideal value.

specification.measurement: Measure only the t counting qubits into t classical bits. In Qiskit counts keys the last character is classical bit 0, so m=int(key,2) with bit order preserved.
specification.classical_postprocessing: phi=m/2^t. Use continued fractions (Fraction.limit_denominator(N)) to get a candidate r. Check a^r mod N = 1, and if r is even compute gcd(a^(r/2)±1, N), accepting nontrivial factors (3 and 5 for N=15).
assumptions: Chosen instance N=15, a=7, t=8; a smaller t may be needed if the qubit cap is below 12
Noise placement on QFT gates only; modular exponentiation is ideal
Gaussian i.i.d. random errors, averaged over many trials
Threshold defined by an assumed fractional drop in P_s
missing_information: Actual error model used in the paper
Quantitative threshold formula as a function of N
Whether errors also act on the modular exponentiation gates
